children: has embraced the rapid rise of agentic AI, releasing new chips specifically built to run agents and AI tools on smartphones during its Snapdragon Summit in Hawaii on Tuesday.

The company revealed its latest mobile offerings, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 Mobile Platform and the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Mobile Platform. Both platforms are aimed at the newest models of smartphones and are built on the 2nm process node. They include Qualcomm's Oryon CPU, a rearchitected Qualcomm Adreno GPU, and an updated Hexagon NPU.

"These are two chips that go into the high-end smartphone market," said Qualcomm CFO and COO Akash Palkhiwala during a roundtable discussion with reporters on Tuesday. "They have best-in-class performance on gaming and productivity. These also set up the platform for agentic AI."
This means the devices will be able to provide high performance for running AI agents, such as Meta's
Spark. He also indicated these on-device agents are just the start.

"For phones, Gemini and then Muse, a smart agent that can sit on the phone, gather information, and take action," Palkhiwala said. "Several Chinese phones will also be taking part. There are several more companies looking to launch similar agents. We think this proliferation will create a lot of new use cases."
Personal AI agents won't only appear in consumers' smartphones but also in automotive, home devices and other types of wearable tech products.
When using agents on a device like a smartphone, Palkhiwala said there is a seamless transition where the tasks can be handled on device or need to access more compute from the cloud.
"The agent on the phone makes the choice," he said. "It also needs to be transparent to the user."

"Today marks a milestone as we introduce not one, but two new flagship mobile platforms, delivering agentic AI experiences that are immediate, personal, and adaptive," said Qualcomm executive Chris Patrick in a statement. "As the agentic AI age evolves, our multi-flagship strategy allows us to push the boundaries of what's possible for mobile while bringing our latest AI innovations to a broader range of premium devices. By designing two innovative platforms, we're giving OEMs greater choice as we collectively shape the capabilities of the next generation of intelligent, personalized, mobile experiences."

"AI is evolving from a tool that responds into an intelligent collaborator that can understand intent, take action and help get things done," said Clare Conley, vice president of public relations at Qualcomm. "As agents become part of our daily lives, Snapdragon is uniquely positioned to power intelligent, seamless experiences across the personal devices people use every day, from earbuds and smartphones to PCs and cars."
The new chips are part of Qualcomm's three-headed strategic transformation, which includes data center expansion, full-stack physical AI solutions, and integrated hardware-software platforms.
"We have a very broad portfolio through the devices and in the data center," Palkhiwala said. "We can play on both sides, which is very attractive for us."
The Snapdragon Summit continues through Thursday, Sept. 24.
